# Checkpoint — Lukas Maar / 深度对话与自述

## Identity
- Homepage https://lukasmaar.github.io/ self-describes: Security Researcher at Calif; Senior Security Researcher at ISEC, TU Graz; PhD in CS 2025 under Stefan Mangard.
- Focus self-stated: kernel exploitation, defenses, side channels for Linux and Android kernels.
- Consistent with person_json (内核侧信道与移动端漏洞; Black Hat US/Asia; 直接漏洞发现与利用). GitHub `lukasmaar`, TU Graz email `lukas.maar@tugraz.at`.

## Confirmed primary sources (WebFetch-read)
1. https://lukasmaar.github.io/ — homepage bio/affiliation/education/talk list (primary).
2. https://lukasmaar.github.io/posts/heap-kaslr-leak/index.html — self-narrated origin, methodology, disclosure, publishing motivation (primary).
3. https://lukasmaar.github.io/posts/qaic-page-uaf/index.html — self-narrated hardware-virtualization workaround + self-attribution of exploit (primary).

## Key self-narrated claims captured
- Origin: 2023 discussion with Daniel Gruss → "kernel resembles hardware" reframing → 2024 KernelSnitch direction.
- Method: manual kernel hash-table auditing via Bootlin + CodeQL ("old-school code archaeology").
- Iteration: cross-version experimentation toward a universal, system-independent workflow.
- Disclosure: KernelSnitch responsibly disclosed three times (pre-NDSS, post-Nullcon Berlin, to Google).
- Publishing motive: transparency + defensive research support.
- Constraint tooling: virtualized QAIC driver in QEMU due to lack of accelerator hardware.
- Self-attribution: "I found the vulnerability and developed the exploit myself"; AI (Codex) only for auxiliary build/virtualization.
- Mentorship: PhD under Stefan Mangard at TU Graz ISEC (2025).
